VERDICT (phase-417 gap-verdict pass, 2026-09-21) — ADOPT-BOUNDED. The reason above holds; what it does not say is WHY this is not the same one-liner as the C++ half, and the difference is the receiver. Our Rust entity handle is a bare arena index with no back-reference — `PublisherHandle { index: usize, _marker }` (`nros-node/src/publisher.rs:10`) — so rclrs's `&self`-only signature cannot reach the string; the name lives in the arena entry, beside the `topic_name` the C `rcl_publisher_t` stores. ADOPT-BOUNDED is the honest disposition: take upstream's NAME, on a signature that also takes the node or executor the handle indexes into. The weakening is visible — the compiler demands the argument, which is RFC-0089's mechanical-edit test — and it is forced by the fixed-arena model of RFC-0002, not chosen.

VERDICT (phase-444, 2026-09-21) — DIVERGENCE, for the reason `rust:Publisher::topic_name` states in full, and with the same correction: the ADOPT-BOUNDED premise (an arena index needing the node passed in) was measured and is false. `NodeHandle::create_client` returns `EmbeddedServiceClient`, which owns a `CffiClient` whose `service_name()` has been there all along (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs:4581`, `:4712`).

SHIPPED, in one sweep over the whole entity-handle class: `EmbeddedPublisher::topic_name`, `EmbeddedRawPublisher::topic_name`, `Subscription::topic_name`, `RawSubscription::topic_name`, `EmbeddedServiceServer::service_name`, `EmbeddedServiceClient::service_name`, `RawServiceServer::service_name` and `RawServiceClient::service_name` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/handles.rs`). Upstream's verb, upstream's `&self`, no node argument and no arena lookup — each is a one-line forward to the backend handle that has retained the name since it was created.

WHAT IS LEFT IS THE RECEIVER, and `rust:Client` / `rust:Service` already say what it is: rclrs's `Client` is a handle a live node hands back, ours splits into `ServiceClient` (the entity a component DECLARES, RFC-0043/0044) and `ClientTrait` (the RMW seam), with the live handle a third name again, `EmbeddedServiceClient`. No type of ours keys as `Client` or `Service`, so no implementation can close these two rows; what an implementation CAN do, and now has, is make sure the capability is not the thing missing. The C++ halves — `cpp:Client::get_service_name` and `cpp:Service::get_service_name` — did close on this commit and are deleted, because there our class IS `rclcpp::Client`.

NOT ON THE `nros_rmw` TRAIT, which is the one real decision here. `MetadataPublisher` is a ZST and `ZenohPublisher` stores no name, so a required trait method would make every backend keep a SECOND 256-byte copy of a string the C-ABI shim above it already holds, on targets that count bytes. `actual_qos` (issue 1437) IS on the trait because only a backend can answer it; a name is handed IN at create and retained one layer up.
